input.quote: This Agreement shall become effective on the Effective Date and shall continue for a period of three (3) years unless terminated as provided in Section 5.0. This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs for a committed three-year initial term (p0104) and Section 5.0 permits termination by either Party only "for cause" — uncured material breach, insolvency events, acquisition by a competitor, or continuing force majeure (p0107, p0110-p0118). There is no termination-for-convenience right for IBM at the Agreement level, so IBM is locked into a multi-year term, which the playbook treats as walk-away territory and the detection guidance flags as a deviation (missing behaviour). The six-month notice in Section 4.0 is only a non-renewal right at the end of a term, not a convenience exit during the term, and IBM's Purchase Order cancellation right (p0722) is order-level only and remains subject to cost reimbursements. MSL likewise has no convenience right, so the redline adds an IBM-only 30-day convenience termination with refund of prepaid amounts (preferred position) while confirming MSL cannot walk away mid-term; we can fall back to 60-90 days' notice if MSL needs transition runway.

ops.text: 5.4 Termination for Convenience. IBM may terminate this Agreement, or any Purchase Order or portion of the Work hereunder, for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL, without payment of any termination fee or penalty. Upon such termination, MSL shall promptly refund to IBM any amounts prepaid by IBM for periods after the effective date of termination, and the Parties' respective rights and obligations with respect to Products, Parts and inventory shall be determined in accordance with Sections 5.2 and 5.3. MSL shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the initial term or any renewal term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a convenience exit for IBM on thirty (30) days' notice with a refund of prepaid amounts, because Section 5.0 currently permits termination only for cause during a three-year committed term. Our playbook requires a customer convenience right; we can discuss 60-90 days' notice if MSL needs more transition runway.
proposal.summary: Add an IBM termination-for-convenience right (30 days' notice) with refund of prepaid amounts; MSL retains no convenience right.
